findings.F1: In folds B and C, the tested dip measure predicts the next 5 days only in calm markets. With the trend measured on the 60-day return, the slope of the 5-day excess return on the depth below the 5-day high is 0.047 in rising calm (t 3.13, 182 cases), 0.039 in choppy calm (t 2.70, 99 cases) and 0.024 in falling calm (t 2.15, 161 cases). It is only 0.028 in rising agitated (t 1.38, 136 cases) and 0.008 in falling agitated (t 0.98, 240 cases). This is the opposite of the brief's recovery: deeper dips are followed by lower returns than usual.
findings.F2: The rising calm result holds when the trend is read on the 30-day return: slope 0.037, t 3.09, 235 cases, against slope 0.017, t 1.35, 211 cases in rising agitated.
findings.F3: In rising markets the effect is graded across the five depth fifths. The mean 5-day excess return runs -3.0 % (t -1.57), +0.8 %, +1.0 %, +2.7 % (t 1.78) and +4.6 % from the deepest dip to the 5-day high, 318 cases.
findings.F4: Much of the rising calm gradient comes from the high end, not the deep end. Cases at the 5-day high gain +4.8 % over 5 days above drift (t 2.13, 63 cases). The deepest fifth loses only -2.4 % (t -1.17).
findings.F5: Over all coins and profiles in folds B and C, the dip slope is 0.016 (t 2.59, 1422 cases) and positive in 9 of 12 windows. On all four folds the verdict found only t 1.08, so the effect over every market is weak and uneven.
findings.F6: The other angles show nothing that stands out from chance given how many were looked at:

ideas.idea: In a rising, calm market, the further a coin's close sits below its highest close of the past 5 days, measured against its usual daily swing over the past 30 days, the weaker its return over the next 5 days, so that the coins closest to their 5-day high gain the most.
ideas.consequence: In a steady, low-swing uptrend, a coin's few-day pullback in swing units is a reason to refuse buying the dip and to prefer the coins holding near their recent high for the next five days.
ideas.name: rising calm dip underperforms
